title: Contradictory terms evaluate to false
statement: Let $t$ be a term (a conjunction of literals) over the variables $x_0,\dots,x_{n-1}$. If $t$ contains two literals on the same variable with opposite polarities — one negated and one not — then $t$ evaluates to false under every assignment $x : \{0,\dots,n-1\} \to \{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}$.
hypotheses_covered: t is a term over n variables
t contains two literals on the same variable with opposite polarities (termHasContradiction t = true)
x is an arbitrary assignment of the n variables
replaced:
If $\mathrm{termHasContradiction}\,t = \texttt{true}$, then for every input $x$ the term
evaluates to false under conjunction: $\mathrm{Term.eval}\,t\,x = \texttt{false}$.
